issues.legal_issue: Land lawfully held or occupied and used for a sugar factory, other than land held or occupied for cultivation or consisting of groveland, forms part of the scheduled undertaking and vests upon acquisition.
material_facts: The landowners had leased the land to a sugar mill before the relevant acquisition legislation came into force.
The mill lawfully held and occupied the land under the lease and used it to park vehicles bringing sugarcane to the factory.
The land was not being used for cultivation and was not groveland.
The mill was a scheduled undertaking, and the statutory appointed day had occurred.
issues.conclusion: The land vested in the State Government under the acquisition legislation; vesting was not limited to the leasehold interest.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 2(h)(vi) and 3 of the Uttar Pradesh Sugar Undertakings (Acquisition) Act, 1971, a scheduled undertaking includes land, other than land held or occupied for cultivation and grovelands, held or occupied for the factory's purposes, including land held under lease. The word “held” encompasses lawful possession backed by a right or title and is not confined to ownership. The Court relied on State of U.P. v. Lakshmi Sugar & Oil Mills Ltd. (2013) 10 SCC 509; Reserve Bank of India v. Peerless General Finance and Investment Co. Ltd. (1987) 1 SCC 424; A.G. Varadarajulu v. State of T.N. (1998) 4 SCC 231; and the interpretations of “held” in State of U.P. v. Sarjoo Devi (1977) 4 SCC 2, Bhudan Singh v. Nabi Bux (1969) 2 SCC 481, State of A.P. v. Mohd. Ashrafuddin (1982) 2 SCC 1, and Hari Ram v. Babu Gokul Prasad (1991 Supp (2) SCC 608).

rule.if: factory_acquisition_vesting_appeal and land_lawfully_held_or_occupied and land_used_for_factory_purpose and not land_used_for_cultivation and not land_is_groveland

predicates.factory_acquisition_vesting_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning whether land used by a sugar factory forms part of an acquired undertaking.
predicates.land_lawfully_held_or_occupied: The factory lawfully held or occupied the land under a right or title, including a lease.
predicates.land_used_for_factory_purpose: The factory used the land for a purpose of its operations.
predicates.land_used_for_cultivation: The land was held or occupied for cultivation.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns vesting of factory land, land lawfully held or occupied and used for the factory, if neither used for cultivation nor groveland, is treated as part of the undertaking and vests in the state.

issues.legal_issue: Land used for non-agricultural purposes before the agricultural land regime commenced does not vest under that regime merely because a lease of the land is said to contravene its restrictions, and the owners are not thereby barred from pursuing a compensation remedy.
material_facts: The lease of the land to the sugar mill predated the commencement of the Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950.
The land was being used for non-agricultural purposes before that Act came into force, including parking vehicles bringing sugarcane to the factory.
An authority made a declaration under Section 143 that the land was being used for non-agricultural purposes, based on an earlier official report.
The High Court had relied on Sections 156 and 167 to find that the lease was void, the land vested under the 1950 Act, and the owners lost their rights.
issues.conclusion: The land did not vest in the Government under the 1950 Act, and the owners were not disentitled from pursuing any available remedy for compensation.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(14) of the Uttar Pradesh Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950 defines land by reference to land held or occupied for purposes connected with agriculture, horticulture, or animal husbandry. The Court held that the Act did not apply to land already used for non-agricultural purposes before its commencement, particularly in light of the declaration under Section 143; Sections 156 and 167 therefore did not establish vesting or extinguish the owners' ability to pursue compensation. The Court did not decide the amount or ultimate entitlement to compensation.

rule.if: agricultural_land_vesting_dispute and land_leased_before_regime_commenced and land_used_for_nonagricultural_purposes_before_regime and nonagricultural_use_formally_declared

predicates.agricultural_land_vesting_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether land vested under a regime governing agricultural land.
predicates.land_leased_before_regime_commenced: The landowners leased the land before the agricultural land regime commenced.
predicates.land_used_for_nonagricultural_purposes_b: The land was used for purposes outside agriculture, horticulture, and animal husbandry before the regime commenced.
predicates.nonagricultural_use_formally_declared: A competent authority formally declared that the land was being used for non-agricultural purposes.

issues.definition: In a dispute over vesting under an agricultural land regime, if land was leased and used non-agriculturally before the regime commenced and that use was formally declared, the owners may pursue an available compensation remedy.
